In \(\triangle ABC\), seg AB \(\cong\) seg AC, so by the isosceles triangle theorem the angles opposite them are congruent, that is \(\angle ABC = \angle ACB\). Hence \(x = 50^\circ\).
In \(\triangle DBC\), seg BD \(\cong\) seg CD, so likewise \(\angle DCB = \angle DBC\). Hence \(y = 60^\circ\).
Since point A is above seg BC and point D is below it, \(\angle ABD = \angle ABC + \angle DBC = 50^\circ + 60^\circ = 110^\circ\) and \(\angle ACD = \angle ACB + \angle DCB = 50^\circ + 60^\circ = 110^\circ\).
Hence \(x = 50^\circ\), \(y = 60^\circ\), \(\angle ABD = 110^\circ\) and \(m\angle ACD = 110^\circ\).

The median drawn to the hypotenuse of a right angled triangle is half the hypotenuse. So the median \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 15 = 7.5\).
Hence the length of the median of the hypotenuse is 7.5.

In \(\triangle PQR\), \(\angle Q = 90^\circ\), so seg PR is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras' theorem, \(PR^2 = PQ^2 + QR^2 = 12^2 + 5^2 = 144 + 25 = 169\), so \(PR = 13\).
QS is the median drawn from Q, so S is the midpoint of the hypotenuse PR. The median on the hypotenuse of a right angled triangle is half the hypotenuse, so \(l(QS) = \frac{1}{2} \times 13\).
Hence \(l(QS) = 6.5\).

The point of concurrence of the medians of a triangle divides each median in the ratio \(2 : 1\) from the vertex. Here seg PT is the median drawn from P and G is that point of concurrence, so \(PG : GT = 2 : 1\).
Therefore \(PG = 2 \times GT = 2 \times 2.5 = 5\).
Since P - G - T, \(PT = PG + GT = 5 + 2.5 = 7.5\).
Hence PG = 5 and PT = 7.5.
